notes.title: -(으)ㄹ 정도로
notes.text: -(으)ㄹ 정도로 means "so much that…, to the point of…": 눈물이 날 정도로 고마워요 (I'm so grateful I could cry), 잠을 못 잘 정도로 걱정돼요 (I'm so worried I can't sleep). Money verbs: 돈을 벌다 (earn), 모으다 (save up), 마련하다 (get together, raise).

notes.title: Big numbers
notes.text: Korean counts in units of 만 (10,000): 십만 (100,000), 백만 (1,000,000), 천만 (10,000,000). So 천만 원 is ten million won. Rough numbers: 한두 (one or two), 두세 (two or three), 서너 (three or four), 몇십 (several dozen). 이상 = or more, 이하 = or less.

notes.title: Units
notes.text: Korea uses the metric system: 그램 (g), 킬로그램 or 킬로 (kg), 밀리미터 (mm), 킬로미터 (km), 톤 (ton). At the market you buy meat by weight: 돼지고기 오백 그램 주세요. A 자가용 is a privately owned car; 승용차 is any passenger car.

scene.ko: 음… 좀 써. 토마토가 덜 익었나 봐. 식품은 질이 제일 중요해.

notes.title: -는 대신(에)
notes.text: -는 대신에 means "instead of" or "in exchange for": 택시를 타는 대신에 걸었어요 (I walked instead of taking a taxi), 내가 요리하는 대신에 설거지는 네가 해 (I'll cook, and you do the dishes in exchange). With nouns: 커피 대신 차 (tea instead of coffee). Water is always free at Korean restaurants — often self-service.

notes.title: Trade words
notes.text: 수입 has two meanings: "import" (輸入) and "income" (收入) — context tells you which. 수출 = export, 무역 = trade, 소비자 = consumer, 부동산 = real estate, 주택 = housing. Seoul home prices are one of the hottest topics in Korean news.

notes.title: N만큼
notes.text: N만큼 means "as … as N": 할머니 김치만큼 맛있어요 (as tasty as Grandma's kimchi), 생각만큼 비싸지 않아요 (not as expensive as I thought). 그만큼 = that much. 맨 (the very — 맨 앞, 맨 뒤) and 온 (the whole — 온 가족, 온 동네) go before nouns. Food trucks and night markets pop up along the Han River in summer and fall.
